subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Key studies: Freud (Little Hans); Siffre cave study

questions.q: Approximately how long is one full human circadian rhythm?
questions.explain: Circadian rhythms are biological cycles that repeat roughly every 24 hours.

questions.q: What name is given to internal biological clocks that help regulate the sleep-wake cycle?
questions.explain: Endogenous pacemakers are the body's internal clocks that control biological rhythms.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an exogenous zeitgeber?
questions.explain: Exogenous zeitgebers are external cues such as light that help set the internal clock.

questions.q: During which stage of sleep does most vivid dreaming typically occur?
questions.explain: Vivid dreaming is most strongly associated with rapid eye movement (REM) sleep.

questions.q: The restoration explanation of sleep proposes that sleep functions mainly to:
options: Allow the body and brain to repair and recover
questions.explain: Restoration theory views sleep as a time for the body and brain to repair and recover.

questions.q: Which of the following is a proposed function of sleep?
questions.explain: Restoration is a commonly proposed function of sleep, alongside protection and survival.

questions.q: According to Freud's psychodynamic theory, dreams are primarily a form of:
questions.explain: Freud argued that dreams represent the unconscious fulfilment of wishes and desires.

questions.q: In Freud's theory, the 'manifest content' of a dream is:
options: The events the dreamer actually remembers
The random signals from the brainstem
The external cues that trigger sleep
questions.explain: Manifest content is the literal storyline of the dream that the person recalls.

questions.q: In Freud's theory, the 'latent content' of a dream refers to:
questions.explain: Latent content is the disguised unconscious meaning that lies behind the dream.

questions.q: Freud used the term 'dream work' to describe the process that:
options: Converts latent content into manifest content
questions.explain: Dream work transforms the hidden latent content into the remembered manifest content.

questions.q: Who proposed the activation-synthesis theory of dreaming?
questions.explain: Hobson and McCarley proposed the activation-synthesis theory in 1977.

questions.q: According to the activation-synthesis theory, dreams are best described as:
options: The brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during REM sleep
questions.explain: The theory states the brain synthesises random REM activity into a dream narrative.

questions.q: A psychologist argues that dreams carry no hidden meaning and simply reflect the brain interpreting random signals. Which theory does this match?
questions.explain: Activation-synthesis treats dreams as meaningless by-products of random brain activity.

questions.q: A therapist tells a client that their dream about losing teeth secretly represents an unconscious anxiety. Which Freudian concept is being used?
questions.explain: Interpreting a hidden meaning behind the dream reflects Freud's idea of latent content.

questions.q: Insomnia is best described as:
options: Falling asleep uncontrollably during the day
Persistent difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
questions.explain: Insomnia involves ongoing trouble getting to sleep or remaining asleep.

questions.q: Secondary insomnia is insomnia that:
options: Is caused by another condition or factor such as illness or stress
Is caused by sleeping too much
questions.explain: Secondary insomnia results from another underlying problem, unlike primary insomnia.

questions.q: A student drinks several coffees late at night, has an irregular bedtime and now struggles to fall asleep. This suggests insomnia linked to:
questions.explain: Caffeine and an irregular routine are lifestyle factors that can trigger insomnia.

questions.q: In Freud's case study, what was Little Hans afraid of?
questions.explain: Little Hans developed a phobia of horses, which Freud interpreted psychodynamically.

questions.q: In Siffre's cave study, what happened to his sleep-wake cycle when he lived without natural light or clocks?
options: It settled into a cycle of roughly 24-25 hours
questions.explain: Without external cues Siffre's body clock free-ran to a cycle of around 25 hours.

questions.q: Siffre's finding that his rhythm continued in roughly 24-25 hour cycles underground is used as evidence that:
options: Sleep is controlled only by external light
The sleep-wake cycle is partly controlled by internal endogenous pacemakers
questions.explain: The rhythm persisting without cues shows an internal biological clock helps drive it.
